title: Trax machine glossary, version 1
description: What the words of a set of Gherkin features mean: the actors (each with the noun a feature names a person by: `Ada is a customer`), the machines with the noun or name a feature refers to them by, states, triggers, guards, invoked trains and links, and the views. Machines are derived from the features and this file (Trax.Docs/adr/0058). Normative: the C# reader accepts exactly the documents this schema accepts, then refuses the ones whose names do not agree (a phrase used twice, an owner that is not an actor); the corpus under formats/glossary holds the two to each other. Every object is closed. The field, rule and reduction shapes are the IR's own.

phrase.description: Words a step is written in. Compared with case and runs of whitespace ignored.

word.description: A lowercase name: an actor, a guard.

machineId.description: A machine's id, lowercase words joined by single hyphens, so no two ids emit the same type names.

member.description: A state or trigger name, emitted as an enum member.

systemKey.description: The fixed key of a system instance: the machine id, a slash, and a name.

actor.description: An actor, and the noun a feature names a person by: `Given Ada is a customer`. It holds roles, or says it is any signed-in caller; never neither.

machine.description: One machine. A user's machine is owned by an actor and has a noun (`order`: a feature says `Ada's order`, or `her order` for the step's own person); a system machine has a fixed key and a name (`the shop`). Never both.

ownedBy.description: The actor whose people own its instances, or several: each person owns their own, and each trigger is granted the actors the features show firing it.

system.description: A system machine: the fixed key of its one instance, which the host starts, or { "keyedBy": [...] }, one instance per key, which host code starts and moves and a step names by its name and key (ticket "T-12"). No view reads and no policy moves a keyed one.

version.description: The machine's definition version, which its snapshots carry and a migration steps from. Defaults to 1.

start.description: What follows a person's name to give them a new instance: `has an order`.

initialContext.description: The context a new instance starts with. Without it, each field of the initial state's context starts at its zero (null for a nullable one).

differential.description: Write the IR's differential block from the scenarios: each input a served trigger is sent with, each output an outcome is given, and each context a Given sets an instance up in.

rules.description: Each custom rule the machine names, by its name in the IR.

reductions.description: Each custom reduction the machine names, by its name in the IR.

migrations.description: The IMachineMigration class of each version step below the machine's version, by the version it steps from.

state.description: A state with more than its phrase: committed (only the effect runner enters it, and a save never leaves it), the rule its context must meet, and a context of its own in place of the machine's.

trigger.description: A trigger and its phrase. A person's act is the phrase after their name (`places {subject}`); anything else is the whole step (`{subject} starts baking`, `the shop opens`). `{subject}` is where a user machine's instance is named, and every other {placeholder} names an input field. A trigger with an `effect` is sent by its instance's owner with no input of theirs: the server runs the effect, then fires the trigger with the effect's receipt (`input.receipt`).

guard.description: The guard that decides the trigger when more than one guard tells its moves from its refusals: it must hold on every move and fail on every refusal.

effect.description: The run-once effect a send of the trigger runs: its ISnapshotEffect interface (written to the host file), the key prefix its claims are taken under (the IR's, `<machine>:<Trigger>` when not given), and the receipt an in-memory run answers with.

customRule.description: A custom rule's ICustomRule class (written to the host file) and whether an in-memory run takes it to hold. A scenario that needs the real rule is tagged @host.

customReduction.description: A custom reduction's ICustomReduction class (written to the host file) and the context fields an in-memory run sets in its place. A scenario that needs the real reduction is tagged @host.

guard.description: A condition, with the words a Given or a Then says it holds or fails in. A guard whose rule reads only the trigger's input is shown by a When's value and may leave `holds` and `fails` out; the C# reader refuses one that reads the context without both.

invoke.description: The train a state invokes (keyed by the state), what it is given, what it answers, and the words for each outcome.

train.description: The train's canonical name, its interface's full name (Trax.Docs/adr/0007).

input.description: Each field of the train's input, by name, from the context field named, or from "$owner": the instance owner's qualified principal id, which the server sets and no client can write. A system machine has no owner, and no context field may be named "$owner".

examples.description: An output for each done outcome, by its phrase, that a scenario run in memory answers with.

link.description: Keyed by its phrase, which names another machine's instance at `{subject}` (`the receipt for {subject}`): the instance whose id this machine's context field holds.

view.description: A view: what it reads (the caller's own instances of a user machine, a system instance at its key) and the fields it shows.

viewField.description: One shown field: a machine's state, or one of its context fields. A state may be shown with a label per state.
